title: Coverage report freshness command ignores its status source

evidence.quote: Report records status_source but freshness_audit_command hard-codes --input artifacts/sync-status.json.
Semester maintenance passes paths.status as the coverage statusSource.

reasoning: buildTermCoverageReport tracks the actual status source, but the generated freshness audit command always uses artifacts/sync-status.json. In the semester maintenance flow the status file is written under the selected output directory, so the coverage artifact can instruct operators to audit a stale or nonexistent global file rather than the status snapshot used to build the plan.
reproduction: Run the semester maintenance plan with a custom outputDir, then inspect term-coverage-plan.md; Status source points at the bundle's sync-status.json, while the Freshness Gate command still uses artifacts/sync-status.json.
recommendation: Build freshness_audit_command from statusResult.source or args.statusInput when available, and shell-quote the selected status and retention paths. Keep artifacts/sync-status.json only as a fallback when no source path exists.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Coverage tests assert the command includes --min-historical-terms or --retention-input, and semester tests assert report.status_source, but none assert that the generated --input path matches status_source.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a buildTermCoverageReport test with statusSource: 'bundle/sync-status.json' and retentionSource set, then assert freshness_audit_command contains --input bundle/sync-status.json.
minimumFixScope: scripts/term-coverage-plan.ts command construction, with one focused term coverage test.
